matching_bullets: Meta ships a terminal coding agent in beta while a smaller one relicenses to sell the layer above it
verifications.reason: Genuinely borderline, so recorded as such rather than resolved in either direction. Real orchestration-ness is present and it is the reported substance rather than incidental: Muse Code's subagents are asynchronous and persist for the whole session rather than being spawned per task and decide themselves when to report back, and every model call, tool run, approval and edit is appended to a local event log that Meta describes as making the agent replay-exact and restart-safe — which is the durable-execution property that the rubric's own named siblings Restate and Temporal exist to sell, and 'multi-step agent' is in the row's generic list. Herdr adds a second and distinctly weaker orchestration surface, a runtime that organises command-line agents into panes, tabs and projects and keeps them running persistently on whichever machine it is installed on, including a remote host it installs itself onto over ssh — but the post is explicit that those machines are disconnected from each other today, so the cross-machine orchestration that would have strengthened this row is a named future commercial feature rather than shipped behaviour. Against that, no workflow or pipeline platform shipped anything today — no n8n, Inngest, Prefect, Dust.tt, Flowise or Langflow state change — and both hits arrive as architecture inside coding-agent products whose primary row is Agent Harness. Orchestration-ness yes, workflow-platform-ness no.

A token scan of every category, body, citation label and URL returns zero hits for Multica and zero for any profile or multi-profiling concept. This is the news-driven-only topic and nothing today triggers it. The one item considered and rejected is the Unsloth bullet's DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 quantisation ladder from 83 GB at UD-IQ1_S to 162 GB at UD-Q8_K_XL: that is a set of size-accuracy SKUs of a single model, which the rubric places under Local LLM Models as a quantization release, not per-profile model management or profile switching on local hardware. Absence is correct rather than a miss.

verifications.reason: The strongest coverage of the day and a direct hit on the row's generic scope of AI coding agent, agentic IDE and autonomous developer loop, with the rubric's clause about newly entering coding agents applying to both vendors even though neither is on the 2026 brand list. Muse Code is a terminal coding agent, explicitly in beta, installed on macOS and Linux from an install script, built to plan changes, write code and validate the result across large repositories while coordinating specialised subagents, with Muse Spark 1.2 as the coding-focused model underneath. Herdr is the harness layer above the harness: a terminal runtime for command-line coding agents that organises them into panes, tabs and projects and keeps them running persistently on whichever machine it is installed on, including a remote host it installs itself onto over ssh, though the post is explicit that those machines are disconnected from each other today; it was relicensed AGPL to Apache-2.0 on joining Y Combinator's F26 batch. The Scale X study reaches the topic secondarily from the operator side rather than the product side, since its subject is the approve-or-deny prompt that sits inside a coding agent's tool loop, with npm run analyze as the single most-missed command.

verifications.reason: Two independent hits on the row. LFM2.5-2.6B is a model card publication on Hugging Face: 2.6 billion parameters, pre-trained on roughly 34 trillion tokens with the context window extended to 128K mid-training, published with a benchmark table reporting 77.83 on ToolSandbox against 65.00 and 52.40 for the two Gemma 4 comparisons, a Claw-Eval English average of 62.85, and claimed leads on IFBench, Multi-IF and IFStruct — all vendor-measured and not independently reproduced, which the bullet states. The Unsloth bullet carries the quantization-release half of the row, which the rubric lists as its own generic form: DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 quantisations from 83 GB at UD-IQ1_S to 162 GB at UD-Q8_K_XL, plus support for Moonshot's Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 104 billion active parameters, native vision and a one-million-token context window. Those quantisations are scored here rather than against the Unsloth optimisation row, per the rubric's category assignment.

Three PyPI releases landed on Thursday, August 6 — 2026.8.5, 2026.8.6 and 2026.8.7 — after 2026.8.3 on Tuesday and 2026.8.4 on Wednesday, five packages in three days, with the changelog logging 2026.8.3 and 2026.8.6 as fixes only, 2026.8.4 as training fixes and 2026.8.5 as Windows installation fixes, and 2026.8.7 adding DSpark support for DeepSeek-V4 Flash 0731 plus a full rework of the training page. Training fixes and a training-page rework are fine-tuning-tooling news on their own merits; the bullet's own verdict that this is a maintenance cadence rather than a capability one does not make it uncovered.

verifications.reason: Judged on security-ness rather than on the vendor list, and the Scale X study is the centre: it measures the human approval gate in an agent's tool loop across more than 40,000 runs and roughly 409,000 approve-or-deny decisions, with mean accuracy 66.3% and a miss rate that rises the less a hostile command looks hostile — 11.7% for obviously destructive commands, 23.8% for persistent mutation, 33.4% for exfiltration and code execution, 35.0% for scope violations — with 7% of players approving everything. Those categories are the rubric's tool-call abuse, data exfiltration and agent-takeover concepts measured rather than described, and the conclusion that the check belongs in the tool layer where the payload is inspected rather than in the approval prompt where only the command line is, is the row's two sub-bullets stated almost literally: zero-trust access control for agentic AI, and monitoring and managing agent behaviour. Cisco's twelve advisories are product security carrying the same week's operational load, and the events bullet carries the AI-security track in depth including DEF CON's AI Village and HalCTF, an agentic security competition run as a containerised agent contest. The standing AI-security-SoC watch is honoured inside the events bullet, which flags the Hot Chips FPGA session from AMD as the one to watch on the security-silicon intersection.

verifications.reason: The lead bullet is chip-ness end to end and hits the row's specific SKUs and its generic concepts alike. AMD signed a definitive agreement to acquire Taalas, a 2023 Toronto fabless building model-specific integrated circuits that embed a model's weights and dataflow into transistors instead of streaming them from high-bandwidth memory, assembling roughly 100 layers and customising only two metal layers per model at a stated tape-out of about two months; the HC1 test part is on TSMC's 6-nanometer process and served Llama 3.1 8B at roughly 17,000 tokens per second. AMD says it intends to fold the technology into its accelerator roadmap and pair it with Instinct GPUs, Helios rackscale systems, EPYC CPUs and ROCm — tape-out, process node, fabless entrant, HBM avoidance and named SKU families all in one item. The Liquid AI bullet supplies client and data-centre measurements on Apple M5 Max, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 and a single NVIDIA H100, and the events bullet carries the Hot Chips 2026 programme in detail across CPU, GPU, FPGA, memory, networking and accelerator sessions.

No robotics or embodied-AI state change today, the same call as 2026-08-03, 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 on the same shape of content. Every robot-ness token in the file is carried event-calendar material sitting inside the events bullet: IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026's decision calendar and its December dates at the Santa Clara Convention Center, the Waymo keynote and the automotive session at Hot Chips, the physical AI track among the AI Infra Summit's five tracks, and physical AI in the Ray Summit training-day afternoon. No humanoid, quadruped, VLA policy, manipulation, teleoperation or fleet-deployment news exists outside those calendar lines, and calendar entries belong to the events bullet rather than to this topic.

matching_bullets: AMD agrees to buy Taalas and says it intends to fold model-specific silicon into the Instinct roadmap
An experiment across more than 40,000 runs measures how well humans approve agent commands, and the answer scales with disguise
Meta ships a terminal coding agent in beta while a smaller one relicenses to sell the layer above it
verifications.reason: The AMD-Taalas deal is the standout of the day and does not sit cleanly in any one named row: a general-purpose GPU vendor buying the thesis that competes with general-purpose GPUs, where the model is burned into the transistors and the only remaining variable is cost per token, which is simultaneously chip news, M&A and a statement about where inference economics are heading. The Scale X study is the second, an unusually large measurement of the part of the agent loop that is a person rather than a model, whose transferable finding is an ordering — the further a hostile command sits from the shape people are trained to fear, the more reliably it gets waved through — and which points at the tool layer as the place to put the check. Herdr's AGPL to Apache-2.0 relicense is a third, a licensing move read for what it actually does: the network-use clause that would have obliged a hosted service to publish its source is removed, which both widens adoption of the runtime and reserves the hosted layer as the thing the company intends to sell.
